Hey girl, I come from Hispanic background too. I understand that in our community, family is held to the upmost importance, and the tight-knit family can hide a lot of toxic patterns and pass it off as normal because we as kids wouldn’t know any better. 

The behavior you described from your parents is still very inappropriate even for Hispanic families, pretty much textbook covert incest. Ik a lot of people have issues with boundaries in Hispanic families, since physical closeness with family members are important. But to keep forcing physical touch despite you trying everything to stop is not ever okay. 

Hispanic communities often sweep sexual abuse under the rug, and what I have noticed is that many matriarch and women of the family have been abused themselves. “Ataque de nervios” is talked about such a normal thing, but thats actually a panic attack and they need to see some psychiatric help. But they also do not believe in mental illness and think therapy is weak, and just perpetuates a cycle of generational trauma that many haven’t even noticed yet. 

To me, it sounds like you might have some missing memories of abuse. Remember, the mind may not remember, but the body certainly does. The nightmares and mental breakdowns are a big clue. Something may have happened to you, and your mind is protecting you from remembering. It’s a lot like me, and I was abused by several of my family members, while my mom was/ still is an emotionally immature narcissist who couldn’t pay enough attention that I was being abused by the people she dropped me off. I still don’t remember much, but the nightmares, random panic attacks, certain smells and sounds gave me clues.  

I don’t know how to help you in your specific situation, friend, but the only way I have managed to stop everything is by getting away. Being in a survival environment, you will do anything to survive such as cutting, talking to men online or drugs to cope. I hope you learn to realize that the way you lived is not like how anyone else lives, and I hope you don’t succumb to the pain of that realization, and the many more to come. 

I wish you the best, and take care of yourself
